industry.size: Indian tyre industry revenue ~₹1.36 lakh cr in FY26; the top six makers are ~85% of it (CRISIL, 24-Aug-2026)
industry.fy27: CRISIL (24-Aug-2026): volume growth slows to 4-5% in FY27 (replacement and OEM 4-5% each, exports 3-4%) after 7-8% in FY26; key inputs up 35-40%; natural rubber ~₹275/kg in Jun-2026 vs ~₹220/kg in FY26; operating margin down 200-250 bp to ~11.5-12% in FY27 (from ~14.2%), recovering to 13-13.5% in FY28 if input costs stabilise; 'a cost-pass-through lag rather than a structural profitability reset'; the top six plan ~₹18,000 cr of capex over FY27-28, nearly double the previous two years
industry.rubber: Kottayam RSS-4 ₹27,300 per quintal (₹273/kg) on 3-Sep-2026; global futures ~240 US cents/kg on 1-Sep-2026, near the highest since 2013 (Procurement Resource, 10-Sep-2026). Apollo's own basket: rubber ~₹200/kg in Q4FY26, ~₹225 in Q1FY27, ₹260+ expected in Q2FY27
industry.priceHikes: Industry took 7-9% of price increases by Q1FY27 with more planned in Q2 (CLSA via Moneycontrol, 12-Aug-2026); Apollo ~11% by early August, 15-16% needed; competitors followed with similar magnitude (CFO, 7-Aug-2026)
industry.europe: European replacement market flat to negative for two years (CFO, May-2026); EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese tyres announced in 2026 help mid-tier brands (Q1FY27 call); Apollo is a price follower in Europe given its size; Europe needs smaller price increases for the same raw-material rise because natural rubber is a smaller share
industry.regulation: AIS-142 phase 2 noise norms from H2FY27 push truck OEMs towards radials; DGFT licensing of tyre imports since Jun-2020 limits Chinese imports (CARE); GST cut on tyres (Sep-2025) lifted replacement demand

excluded.TVSSRICHAK: Earnings distorted: FY25 EPS collapsed 81% (to ₹26.9 from ₹141) and its trailing P/E reached ~148x inside the five-year window; on 30-Sep-2026 it still trades on recovering earnings (same exclusion as the MRF and BKT reports)

CEAT is kept, as in those reports: its FY22 peak P/E came from the industry-wide raw-material trough. Sensitivity rows show the set with TVS Srichakra and without CEAT.

moat: Brand and replacement pull
Strong
79% of consolidated revenue from replacement (Q1FY27); TBR replacement share 30%+, PCR 21%+ (internal estimates); BCCI Team India jersey since FY26; Vredestein a premium brand in Europe
Pricing follows the industry, but share in truck tyres was regained in FY26
Scale in India
Strong
Two leading TBR makers with MRF; ~58,000 PCR and 15,000+ TBR tyres a day of India capacity before the AP expansion; India utilisation in the 90s
Scale buys distribution and OEM approvals, not margin
Cost position
Weak
Margins move with rubber and crude like everyone's (11.7% in Q1FY27, 17.6% in FY24); ~50% of raw materials imported
No structural cost edge over MRF, CEAT or JK
Europe
Weak
Europe EBITDA margin 13-15% in FY24-26 vs 16%+ 'earlier normal'; a high-cost Dutch plant had to close (₹1,128 cr of charges in FY25-26)
The European arm has not earned its capital; the fix is under way
Technology and premium mix
Moderate
UHP ~50% of Europe mix; EV platform approvals (BMW, MINI, Genesis, Kia, Mahindra); two global R&D centres
Helps mix; peers have similar programmes
Threats
Chinese imports (capped by DGFT licensing in India, EU anti-dumping in Europe), ~₹18,000 cr of industry capex in FY27-28, OEM price negotiations
Capacity additions can cap pricing once raw materials ease
critiques: Margins revive fully in FY28 on normal costs and Europe restructuring; 13.5x FY28E is attractive against peers.
Pricing power is underpinned by robust demand and >90% utilisation; FY27E EPS raised.
Margin pressure and the capex cycle are risks.
The squeeze is a cost-pass-through lag, not a structural reset; industry margins recover to 13-13.5% in FY28 if inputs stabilise.
Europe has disappointed for five years: margins below the 16% the company calls normal, a ₹1,000 cr plant-closure bill, and a 'high teens' promise still to be earned.
The MD's pay doubled to ₹78 cr (541x the median employee) in a year in which consolidated reported profit rose 22% only thanks to a tax write-back.
